activity.title: The more I see AI move into enterprise, the more I think the biggest constraint is not intelligence. It is execution. Most companies already know what they want to change. The challenge is making that change across Salesforce , NetSuite , SAP , Workday , ServiceNow , and the many dependencies connecting them, without adding more risk along the way. That work still requires a huge amount of specialized knowledge, manual coordination, and institutional memory. And too often, the people responsible for moving the business forward are also spending their time rediscovering why systems were configured a certain way five years ago. This is why Assemble caught my attention. Assemble is building an AI Solutions Engineer for enterprise IT. It maps dependencies across core systems, runs changes from a single interface, and verifies them against a shadow environment before they reach production. The important part is not simply that it can execute faster. It is that execution is designed to be controlled: blast-radius analysis before a change, auditable traces for every action, and a revertible ledger when something needs to be rolled back. I do not see this as replacing the people who understand these systems. I see it as giving those teams a better operating layer, one that helps them spend less time on repetitive implementation work and more time on architecture, judgment, and the projects that actually move the business forward. The organizations that make the most of AI may not be the ones experimenting with the most models. They may be the ones that become best at translating ambition into safe, repeatable execution. Where do you see the biggest constraint today, is it deciding what to change, or navigating the systems required to actually ship it? Assemble is now live at assemble.ai to help enterprise teams integrate, migrate, and operate the systems their businesses already run on. ...more ...more

I would've never guessed that I'd be working for a company like Ditto . It's no surprise that there is an insane startup culture at Cal, where people as young as 17 come up with their own business ideas, fueled by their peers, environment, and opportunities that exist here. When Alex Xiao asked me to come work for Ditto, I thought to myself, "Oh my god. He's just another kid at Berkeley promoting another startup." But I'd soon realize that Ditto was much more than "just a startup." On a surface level, we're redefining how AI interacts with people and the way we connect with one another. But if you ask me what I really think of Ditto, I'd tell you I've been given many firsts here. Travelling to LA with friends, meeting an internet celebrity, and going to a yacht party are just the beginning of the opportunities I had at Ditto. To me, Ditto isn't just a company that I work at; it's a family, and I'm proud to be a part of this. ...more

Just Did It! ✔️ This summer, I worked at Nike as an AI, Data, and Machine Learning Engineering Intern on the AI Platform team at the World Headquarters in Beaverton, Oregon. I had the opportunity to contribute to the development of a widely used business intelligence agent supporting employees across product, design, and business enterprise. I gained valuable hands-on experience with AI engineering, system design, and seeing code come to life in production. Special shoutout to my manager Brooke Waldt , project mentor Mark Labinski , and the rest of the team for all of their support, for helping me grow as an engineer, and for answering all of my many questions! But working on my project wasn’t the only thing I did this summer. Between morning NRC runs, workout classes, intern events, coffee chats, meeting CEO Elliott Hill 👀 , and exploring the beautiful PNW, I got to make the most of both work and play. I even had the chance to participate in an Intern Innovation Sprint with seven other interns (shoutout Team Let's Run It!) where we worked cross-functionally to tackle a real-world opportunity for the business. Of course, this summer wouldn’t have been the same if it weren’t for the people who made this experience so special. I would like to thank my mentor, Anna Zimmerman , for her guidance and support as I navigated a new place, new experiences, and so much growth this summer. The Emerging Talent team also did a spectacular job creating a community for us, from fireside chats to taking us to a Thorns game. There was never a dull moment! And a huge thank you to my recruiter, David Jasso , for giving me the opportunity to experience this summer in the first place. Thank you Nike for bringing my dream of a summer to life! The best 10 weeks ever! ⭐
